title: What Your First Print Will Teach You About Your Own Photos
excerpt: A DPReview writer finally makes a real darkroom print of one of his favorite photos, and the physical print reveals things the screen never could.

title: How Far Can You Push Exposure Before Losing the Subject?
excerpt: Wildlife photographer Somdutt Prasad overexposed his Hokkaido crane series "beyond what felt natural" and turned Japanese red-crowned cranes into ink-wash paintings.

title: Why Boredom Might Be the Best Thing for Your Street Photography
excerpt: Street photography is 95% waiting, says Peter Forsgard. Learning to sit inside the slow hours is what sharpens your eye, and panic shots are where most bad images come from.
